title: Dynamics of local quantum information in random unitary circuits
abstract: The physics of information scrambling in quantum many-body systems is intimately related to thermalisation and emergence of chaos. However, its standard characterisation through bipartite entanglement or operator growth remains inherently coarse-grained, obscuring the spatiotemporal anatomy of how quantum information flows between different regions of the system and across various length scales. In this work, we develop a theory for the dynamics of local information in local random unitary circuits which resolves the fine-grained microscopic structures of local information flow in such systems. Using the framework of information lattice which systematises the information content at each length scale within each subsystem, we identify a distribution of length scales at which information resides and obtain the dynamics of the distribution. For Haar-random circuits with infinite local Hilbert-space dimensions, we map this dynamics onto an exact classical stochastic process which reveals that this distribution is described by a Tracy-Widom form which moves ballistically in time ($ \propto t$) toward larger scales, accompanied by a $\sim t^{1/3}$ broadening. We also find the same qualitative behaviour for random Clifford circuits acting on qubits. The similar scaling behaviour in two rather different settings hints strongly towards the universality of our results. In the case of Clifford circuits, we develop a phenomenological Markov process for the dynamics of the stabiliser generators in a specific gauge which confirms the Tracy-Widom distribution and the $t^{1/3}$ scaling of the fluctuations. Ultimately, our results establish the universal properties of the dynamics of local quantum information in a length scale-resolved fashion and provide a possible route towards bridging exact microscopic theories for information dynamics with emergent hydrodynamic descriptions of information flow.
summary: This work develops a novel framework, the information lattice, to track how local quantum information spreads across different length scales in chaotic quantum systems. By analyzing random unitary circuits, the authors find that this information flow exhibits universal scaling characterized by a Tracy-Widom distribution. This establishes a powerful, fine-grained diagnostic tool for understanding quantum scrambling.
main_problem: The paper addresses the limitation of standard, coarse-grained diagnostics (like bipartite entanglement) in characterizing the fine-grained spatiotemporal flow of local quantum information in out-of-equilibrium many-body systems.
main_result: The dynamics of local information are found to follow a universal scaling law, described by a Tracy-Widom distribution that grows ballistically in time ($\propto t$) with a $\sim t^{1/3}$ broadening, regardless of whether the system is Haar-random or Clifford.
method: The authors develop a theory using an 'information lattice' to track information content at every length scale and location, mapping the dynamics onto an exact classical stochastic process for the infinite-dimensional limit.
model_or_system: The study uses random unitary circuits as minimal models for quantum chaos, specifically examining Haar-random circuits (infinite local Hilbert space) and random Clifford circuits acting on qubits.
key_observables: Local information distribution across length scales, the dynamics of the information lattice, and the resulting Tracy-Widom distribution.
important_parameters: Time ($t$), local Hilbert-space dimension ($q$), and the specific type of random unitary circuit (Haar vs. Clifford).
main_assumptions: Standard diagnostics are too coarse-grained; the local information dynamics can be mapped onto a classical stochastic process, and the results are assumed to be universal across different circuit types.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the information lattice structure and the ballistic growth of information flow ($\propto t$) with $\sim t^{1/3}$ fluctuations.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the information lattice framework to resolve local information flow. It then derives the dynamics for Haar-random circuits, mapping it to a classical stochastic process. Finally, it confirms the universal scaling behavior using random Clifford circuits via a phenomenological Markov process.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, length-scale-resolved measure of information flow that bridges microscopic quantum dynamics with macroscopic, hydrodynamic-like descriptions of scrambling and thermalization.
